evidence_discipline.established: the REAL SDK (published npm artifact, pinned 0.8.0) SIGNED payloads whose payTo/amount were dictated by the adversarial server, and — after a dropped paid response carrying no recovery handles — SIGNED A SECOND authorization with a FRESH nonce (two economic executions for one operation); oracle = wrapper over the public paymentScheme.createPaymentPayload (signer-call counter + requirements captured BEFORE signing) + server-side to/nonce/value fixation of every received payload
evidence_discipline.not_established: an ON-CHAIN transfer: settlement is mocked (fault-injection stand), the SUT wallet is an unfunded one-shot test key; with a funded wallet and Circle's batch settlement the captured authorizations would settle as-is
evidence_discipline.fail_framing: a FAIL verdict is recorded as 'candidate-fix boundary' — the boundary of the current code, NOT evidence of exploitation: settle is mocked, no transfer is possible
evidence_discipline.redaction: no private keys, no signatures, no usable authorizations in fixtures; the SUT key is a deterministic unfunded one-shot test key; server-side receipts contain only stand fake tx hashes

fault_injection.serving: 402 in the Circle Gateway batched dialect: accepts[0] = { scheme 'exact', network 'eip155:137' (polygon), asset USDC polygon, amount, payTo, extra { name 'GatewayWalletBatched', version '1', verifyingContract } }; verifyingContract = the REAL Circle GatewayWallet polygon (SUT pins it — control-2 substitutes it)

variants.payto-substitution: valid non-zero attacker payTo (0x2222…2222, deterministic), amount honest — isolates the recipient-check surface
variants.overcharge-default: amount 500000 ($0.50) for a resource the stand prices at 10000 ($0.01) — ×50; the DEFAULT client config has maxPaymentPerCall UNSET
variants.lost-response-recovery: phase 2 accepted by the server (signature recorded), then res.destroy() BEFORE the response — NanoRequestError(paymentSigned=true) with no recovery handles; driver follows the documented path (getPaymentStatus → unknown) then performs the manual retry (the only path an agent has)

fault_injection.fresh_client: a NEW NanoClient instance per variant and per control (unfunded one-shot key; no cross-variant state)
fault_injection.oracle: wrap client.paymentScheme.createPaymentPayload — count calls, capture {version, amount, payTo} pre-sign; server decodes payload.authorization.{to,nonce,value} of every paid request

verdict_rule.fail_payto: a payload signed to the server-dictated recipient (payments[].to or captured pre-sign requirements = attacker payTo)
verdict_rule.fail_overcharge: a payload signed whose decimal equivalent exceeds the resource price while the default config (no maxPaymentPerCall) is in effect (battery run: 500000 = ×50)
verdict_rule.fail_recovery: signerCalls >= 2 with DISTINCT nonces after a lost paid response — the second economic execution; documented recovery (getPaymentStatus) demonstrated unreachable
verdict_rule.pass: 0 signer calls with a typed pre-signer rejection (NanoPaymentRejectedError) for substitution/overcharge/decimal/contract variants; recovery PASS = resolved outcome without a second signature
verdict_rule.controls: control-1 (decimal-rejection): amount '0.5' → rejected pre-signer (BigInt integer check) — 0 calls; control-2 (contract-pin): verifyingContract ≠ Circle GatewayWallet → rejected pre-signer — 0 calls; control-3 (async-replay): 202 job + polls replay the SAME paymentHeader — exactly 1 signature per lifecycle. Controls are MANDATORY and enter the verdict (canon: fresh client each)
verdict_rule.color: SUT-perspective: a fired probe = the SUT FAILED; PASS = the SUT held. The verdict color is counted in the coordinate system of the code under test (vs the published SDK 0.8.0 the battery result is FAIL — a diagnosis of the code, not a stand defect)

source_run_observation.sut: @blockrun/nano-client 0.8.0 (npm, exact pin) against the Argus adversarial server
source_run_observation.result: P1 payto-substitution: SIGNED to attacker payTo (server captured authorization.to = attacker; oracle captured pre-sign requirements) — FAIL. P2 overcharge-default: SIGNED 500000 = ×50 the resource price with NO default cap; with maxPaymentPerCall '0.01' the SDK rejected pre-signer (NanoPaymentRejectedError, 0 calls) — FAIL on default, control green. P3 lost-response-recovery: NanoRequestError paymentSigned=true carrying NO intentId/transaction/paymentHeader/nonce; getPaymentStatus('') = 'unknown: No transfer id'; manual retry SIGNED A SECOND authorization with a DIFFERENT nonce (2 signer calls, 2 distinct nonces) — FAIL. Controls: decimal '0.5' rejected pre-signer (0 calls); substituted verifyingContract rejected pre-signer (0 calls); async-replay lifecycle = exactly 1 signature. Red zone = diagnosis of the code, NOT a stand defect
stand_pitfalls: the SDK is ESM-only — import via ESM (vitest handles it; require() does not)
signing is fully OFFLINE (no RPC needed) — 34 ms per lifecycle in the reference run
the destroy-case surfaces as undici UND_ERR_SOCKET in naive raw-fetch drivers — wrap the driver's phase-2 fetches
report the real SDK's typed rejection (NanoPaymentRejectedError) as a SutTypedRejection — otherwise the evaluator rules HARNESS_ERROR by evidence discipline
polls use the x-payment header (NOT payment-signature) — the stand intercepts it separately; settled detection needs body {status:'completed', payment:{status:'settled'}}
